name: Focus and Do Not Disturb status
plain: Learns only whether the person has a Focus or Do Not Disturb mode switched on.
meaning: iOS returns a single yes or no. Android returns the interruption filter level with no permission.

android.note: Returns ALL, PRIORITY, NONE or ALARMS; no prompt

ios.note: Boolean only; never the mode name or schedule

limits.headline: Can learn only whether Focus or Do Not Disturb is on, not which mode
limits.user_action: On iPhone you tap Allow on the Focus Status prompt; on Android nothing happens
can: Tell whether a Focus is on, as a yes or no (iPhone)
Check the Do Not Disturb level on Android: all, priority, none or alarms, with no prompt
cannot: See the Focus name or schedule on iPhone
See the Do Not Disturb level on iPhone
limits.reach_label: A yes or no, or a level
limits.differs: iPhone asks first and gives only a yes or no; Android gives the level with no prompt.

story.what_it_is: An app can learn only whether you have a Focus or Do Not Disturb mode on.
story.for_you: A friend's messaging app may show that you have notifications silenced. You never see a prompt. It only tells them you are busy, not why.
story.for_makers: Chat apps use it to set expectations about replies and cut pings. It leaks little, but it still tells the app something about your day. iPhone returns just a yes or no. Android returns the filter level without a prompt.

use_cases.example: A chat app shows a notifications silenced note so friends know you will not answer soon.
A work chat tool holds a message until you are out of Focus.
A game delays a non urgent event notice if the player is in Focus.
A workout app notices that you are in a Fitness Focus and starts tracking.
An ad system avoids showing a pop up when the player is in Do Not Disturb.
A health app knows you are sleeping and holds its reminders.
A fraud team uses odd Focus patterns as a very weak signal.

risks: Can be combined with other signals
story.android_note: Android returns the interruption filter level (all, priority, none or alarms) with no prompt.
story.ios_note: iPhone returns only a yes or no, never the name of the mode or its schedule.

technical_bounds: iOS exposes 1 bit and Android exposes 4 levels
iOS reveals only on or off
Android gives the filter with no prompt

legit_uses: Messaging apps show a busy badge
